- Short sentences, one idea each. Drop articles and filler.
- Never drop "not", "never", "no" or "only". A lost negation costs more than
  every token saved.
- Numbers, paths, commands and errors stay verbatim.
- Plain wording wins when the terse form is not shorter.
- Full sentences for a security risk, a step that cannot be undone, and
  anything that needs the user to decide.
- Keep to the report shape and word cap the brief gives. No preamble, no
  recap, no restating the brief.
<!-- voice:end -->

# do-it: design

A standalone skills repo for Claude Code and OpenCode. It keeps the Doc Cycle's
durable record (plans, ADRs, area contexts, changelog, Jira) and drops the fixed
six-hop chain in favour of a flow that scales with the size of the work.

Status: accepted; first cut built. Decisions are recorded in `docs/adr/`.
Sources compared are listed at the end.

## 1. Problems this solves

From a review of `rshingleton/skills` (the current Doc Cycle):

- Every change pays the full cost. `plan-it` grills "however small the work
  looks"; a one-line fix still needs a plan dir, a phase prompt,
  `execution-notes.md`, `audit-report.md`, a verify pass and a docs commit.
- Six user-run hops, each ending in a mandatory `Next:` and refusing to run
  without the previous file (`verify-it` without a PASS report, `implement-it`
  refusing to suggest audit).
- Code and docs are committed in separate skills; `commit-it` refuses a mixed
  tree, so ADRs and glossary never land with the code they describe.
- `verify-it` deletes the plan dir, then `commit-it` digs `jira.md` out of
  `git show HEAD:`.
- Shared rules (commit prefix, `shortcut:` format, the `Next:` chain) are
  restated in up to 9 places and have drifted (from-jira ADR step vs ADR-0012,
  commit-it README vs ADR-0011, compliance rules vs ADR-0011).
- Two competing planning paths (`to-spec`/`to-tickets` vs `plan-it`) plus
  `wayfinder`, with a README note that they "aren't meant to be mixed".

## 2. Principles

1. **One entry, scaled lanes.** `/do-it` sizes the work and runs only the
   steps that size needs. Every step is still callable directly.
2. **Files are the state, not the transcript.** One state block per work item
   records size, status, approvals, assumptions and the verified baseline, so
   any step resumes in a fresh session (addyosmani, ballet).
3. **Approve once, then run.** After plan approval, build runs every ready
   phase and stops only on defined stop conditions (addyosmani `/build auto`).
4. **Different eyes for audit.** Audit runs in fresh-context subagents that get
   the plan, the diff and the build report, never the build transcript
   (ballet).
5. **Outcome routes the next step.** Each step ends `done | blocked | failed`;
   failed audit loops to build, capped at 3 rounds, then becomes a question
   (ballet).
6. **One always-on core.** The coding posture (minimal, reuse first, surgical,
   verifiable) lives in one file and reaches subagents too (ponytail,
   karpathy).
7. **Each rule has one home.** Skills call skills; shared conventions live in
   one reference file; CI fails on drift (mattpocock ADR-0010 style, ponytail
   copy check).
8. **Assume or ask.** Reversible, low-impact unknowns are recorded as
   assumptions and work continues; irreversible or ambiguous ones stop. The
   user confirms the assumption list at ship (ballet).

## 3. Lanes

`/do-it` reads the request (or an issue / Jira key / existing work id), sizes
it, states the lane in one line and proceeds. The user can override
(`/do-it --lane m`). A lane can be raised mid-flight when scope grows; it is
never lowered silently.

| Lane | Signal | Steps | Files written |
|------|--------|-------|---------------|
| XS | 1-2 files, < ~30 lines, no public API, auth, data, schema or config | build -> self-review -> commit | none |
| S | one coherent change, one session | grill (0-3 Qs) -> plan (single file) -> build -> audit (1 reviewer) -> ship | `docs/planning/<id>.md` |
| M | several phases or seams, may span sessions | grill -> phased plan -> build auto -> audit (fan-out) -> ship | `docs/planning/<id>/` |
| L | bundled or epic-sized | roadmap (roadmap-it) -> one S/M item per slice; `--complete`: finish-it chains them | `docs/roadmap/<slug>.md` (kept) + one plan per slice; a run adds `docs/planning/<slug>.run/RUN.md` |

`/do-it <roadmap> --complete [lite|full|ultra]` runs lane L unattended: one
sweep settles every decision (answered, accepted default, or deferred), then
`finish-it` chains the slices, parks what cannot proceed and stops for the
user only at plan approval and the final review. Hard stops, caps and the
digest are in `skills/finish-it/`.

The XS signal mirrors addyosmani's `/ship` skip rule. Anything touching auth,
payments, data migrations, CI or secrets is at least S regardless of size.

## 4. Work-item state

One frontmatter block per work item, in `docs/planning/<id>.md` (S) or
`docs/planning/<id>/README.md` (M), owned by whichever step is running. The
fields, events and rules are in [STATE.md](../skills/do-it/STATE.md) and the
plan layout in [PLAN-FORMAT.md](../skills/scope-it/PLAN-FORMAT.md); nothing
is committed per phase unless a `--complete` run opted in (ADR
[0002](adr/0002-no-commits-until-ship.md), [0008](adr/0008-opt-in-run-commits.md)).
A run keeps its own record, `<slug>.run/RUN.md`, written only by `work.mjs run`.

Principles behind it:

- A recorded verification is a claim about the code at that moment; re-run it
  only if the code moved (addyosmani).
- Approvals count only when recorded in the block, never inferred from a past chat.
- No `jira.md` stub, no `sources/` move, no separate `execution-notes.md`. Jira
  keys and intake links live in the state block.

## 5. Skills

Every skill is named as an `-it` verb so this repo can be installed beside
mattpocock/skills or rshingleton/skills without name collisions (symlink and
OpenCode installs have no namespace). Renamed from their sources:

| Old | New | Old | New |
|-----|-----|-----|-----|
| issue-it | log-it | research | look-it-up |
| plan-it | scope-it | prototype | sketch-it |
| audit-it | prove-it | handoff | pass-it |
| improve-codebase-architecture | deepen-it | writing-for-agents | skill-it |
| grilling | grill-it | doubt | doubt-it |
| tdd | test-it | compliance | guard-it |
| code-review | review-it | tracker | track-it |
| codebase-design | design-it | core | it-core |
| domain-modeling | name-it | diagnosing-bugs | debug-it |

### Flow (user-invoked, short descriptions)

| Skill | Replaces | Job |
|-------|----------|-----|
| `do-it` | ask-matt router, the `Next:` chain | Size, pick lane, resume from state, run steps |
| `log-it` | issue-it, from-jira intake, todo-it | The one intake and backlog skill: sorts each item into an issue (`docs/issues/` or a remote tracker) or a one-line to-do (`docs/TODO.md`); lists, reviews, closes and promotes both; receives out-of-scope discoveries (`propose_work`). See ADR 0007 |
| `scope-it` | plan-it, from-jira, to-spec, to-tickets | Grill scaled to lane, write plan, optional `--jira` publish |
| `build-it` | implement-it, implement, implement-spec | One phase, or the whole frontier with parallel worktrees; lane M phases run in `it-builder` agents (in place, or in worktrees); never commits |
| `prove-it` | audit-it, code-review gate | Fresh-context fan-out, findings, verdict, loop cap |
| `ship-it` | verify-it + commit-it | Finalize docs, confirm assumptions, one commit only on the user's "do it", push/PR on request |

### Discipline (model-invoked, trigger-rich descriptions)

Rewritten in this repo's own words from mattpocock / the fork's ideas, and
fitted to do-it's conventions (state block, resolved project docs, it-core,
seams agreed in scope-it): `grill-it`, `name-it`, `design-it`, `test-it`,
`debug-it`, `review-it`, `look-it-up`, `sketch-it`, `pass-it`, `skill-it`,
`deepen-it`. None carries more than a few lines of boilerplate in common with
its source.

New or reshaped:

- `setup-it` (typed): one-time per-repo onboarding; detects, proposes
  `.do-it/config.env`, a starter `checks.json` and an `AGENTS.md` section,
  writes only what the user accepts.
- `merge-it`: resolves merge, rebase and cherry-pick conflicts by intent;
  build-it's parallel merges call it.
- `retro-it` (typed): turns repeated mistakes and prove-it's guardrail
  candidates into checks, lint config, standards or issues.

- `it-core`: the always-on posture (section 6). Also loaded as `AGENTS.md`.
- `doubt-it`: adversarial fresh-context check of a claim before acting on it
  (addyosmani doubt-driven-development), used by audit and by build on risky
  steps.
- `track-it`: the issue-tracker seam (local, GitHub, Jira) over a small Node
  CLI, with layered dotenv config. The only skill that knows any tracker;
  others call it (ADR-0003).
- `guard-it`: mechanical checks (hooks) and judgement rules (audit), one
  rule set (ADR-0004).

### Dropped

`ask-matt` (replaced by `do-it`), `to-spec`/`to-tickets` as a parallel path,
`implement-spec` (folded into `build-it`), `resolving-merge-conflicts`
(replaced by `merge-it`), in-progress `review` (duplicates `code-review`),
`write-a-skill` (superseded by `skill-it`), the
`improve-codebase-architecture` sub-files duplicated from `design-it`.
`wayfinder`, `triage`, `teach` and `wizard` are not carried over.

## 6. Core posture (always on)

Merged from ponytail and karpathy, one source file:

- **Think first.** State assumptions. If unclear, name the confusion; apply
  assume-or-ask.
- **Ladder.** Take the first option that fully works: does it need to exist;
  already in this codebase; stdlib or platform; installed dependency; one line;
  otherwise the minimum.
- **Lazy about the solution, never about the change.** Before editing, list
  every place the change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports.
- **Surgical.** Every changed line traces to the request. Remove only orphans
  your change created; mention other dead code, don't touch it. Out-of-scope
  findings go to `log-it`.
- **Verifiable.** Turn the task into a check (bug -> failing test first).
  Non-trivial logic leaves a test.
- **Shortcuts are recorded.** `shortcut: <limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
- **Never cut** validation at trust boundaries, data-loss handling, security,
  accessibility.
- **Close every turn** with what happened, then `Skipped / Not checked / Risk`,
  then the next step.

### Terse internal voice

Text another agent or a script reads (briefs, subagent reports, review
findings, scout notes, state-block free text, script output) is terse and
fixed in shape; anything the user reads stays normal prose. One source,
`skills/it-core/VOICE.md`, reaches agents two ways: `npm run gen` copies it
into each `agents/it-*.md` (`npm run check` fails a missing or stale copy),
and the subagent-start hook appends it for every other subagent type
(general-purpose spawns from `look-it-up`, `design-it`, `map-it`). The hook
skips `it-*` so the block is not paid for twice. OpenCode has no subagent
hook and shares one system prompt, so it gets only the agent-file copy
where agents are installed. Each `it-*` agent has a `## Report` contract
with a word cap, and every skill paragraph that starts a subagent names a
cap (`npm run check` fails one without it). `work.mjs show --brief` prints
status, lane, next moves and blocker only.

Adopted from [caveman](https://github.com/juliusbrussee/caveman)
(research: `docs/research/caveman-source-and-flow.md`):

| Rule | Why |
|------|-----|
| Fixed report shapes and word caps | Its own data: voice alone saves about 3% over "answer concisely"; shape, caps and reading less carry the saving |
| Never drop not, never, no, only; numbers, paths, commands, errors verbatim | A lost negation costs more than every token saved |
| Plain wins when terse is not shorter; full sentences for security, irreversible steps and anything needing the user | Clarity over compression where a misread is expensive |
| "This format overrides any other style instruction" | A user who also installs caveman gets these agents' own format |

Skipped: the proxy, shrink, browse and compress tools (they rewrite what the
user and tools produce, not agent-to-agent text); the per-turn reminder and
mode switching (this posture is injected once per subagent, never per turn);
its savings claims (mostly unproven, research section 7). Effect measured in
`docs/research/caveman-baseline.md`.

## 7. Step contracts

### build-it

- Inputs: state block, phase file (M) or plan (S), repo standards.
- Per phase: `test-it` at agreed seams; after 3 failed fix rounds call
  `debug-it`. No commits: the change stays in the working tree
  (ADR-0002), except run commits in a `--complete` run (ADR-0008).
- Frontier from the state block; parallel phases run on scratch branches in
  worktrees and land with `git merge --squash` + `git reset`, so the user's
  branch only ever sees an uncommitted change. Subagents inherit `it-core` via
  the SubagentStart hook on Claude Code.
- Stop conditions: ambiguity that fails assume-or-ask, a failure after
  diagnosis, a merge break on the integration branch (revert the phase merge,
  mark `blocked`), anything `git revert` cannot undo.
- Output: per-phase report in the state block (`done|blocked|failed`, and
  the verification command that passed).

### prove-it

- Fresh-context subagents in parallel, merged in the main context: Spec and
  Standards (`review-it`), Compliance (`.compliance-rules/`, secrets),
  Architecture (deletion test, seams). Lane S skips Architecture only.
- Finding contract (fork + ponytail): concrete case or no finding; recorded
  decisions and `shortcut:` markers are not findings; numbered Must / Should /
  Nice, one line each (`Must|Should|Nice | file:line | claim | case`, with a
  word cap, after caveman's terse reports); ends with `Verdict:` and
  `Not checked:`.
- Writes `audit` in the state block; the full report goes in
  `audit-report.md` only for lane M.
- FAIL routes back to `build-it` with the numbered Must list; round 3 FAIL
  becomes a user question.

### ship-it

One step, one or two commits:

1. Gate: audit PASS at current HEAD (lane XS: self-review footer instead).
2. Show the assumptions list; user confirms, edits or rejects (rejects go to
   `log-it`).
3. Accept linked ADRs, merge terms into the area's CONTEXT.md, write the changelog entry, offer
   untriggered `shortcut:` markers to `log-it`.
4. Jira: one combined prompt for all keys (comment + resolve), not per key.
5. Delete the planning dir after the user answers, before any commit.
6. One question: commit now (code and docs in one commit) or leave it for
   review. `DO_IT_COMMIT=never` makes ship-it only propose the message. Push
   or PR only on request.

## 8. Packaging: Claude Code and OpenCode

```
do-it/
  AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md        # conventions for working on this repo
  skills/<name>/SKILL.md      # flat, so ../other-skill links survive symlinks
  agents/<role>.md            # it-scout, it-reviewer, it-builder, it-planner, it-skeptic: pinned model and tools
  hooks/
    claude.mjs                # Claude Code entry: session/subagent start, pre/post tool
    lib/                      # host-neutral checks, context, guard decisions
    hooks.json                # plugin hook config
  .opencode/plugins/          # OpenCode plugin over hooks/lib
  .opencode/command/*.md      # generated from skills, never hand-edited (OpenCode 1)
  .opencode/commands/*.md     # same files for OpenCode 2
  .opencode/agents/*.md       # generated from agents/: deny-first permission map, no model
  .claude-plugin/             # plugin.json, marketplace.json
  scripts/
    install.sh                # symlinks + hook registration (hooks on by default)
    install-hooks.mjs         # idempotent settings merge, with backups
    gen-opencode.mjs          # skills -> OpenCode commands, agents -> OpenCode agents (--check for drift)
    check.mjs                 # frontmatter, -it names, "Use when", line budget, skill calls, spawn caps, links, em-dashes, agent files and tools
  tests/                      # node --test, no dependencies
  docs/DESIGN.md, docs/adr/
```

- Install: `scripts/install.sh` for both hosts (OpenCode reads
  `~/.agents/skills`), from a clone or piped from curl (it clones or pulls
  `~/.local/share/do-it`, then runs the clone's copy); the Claude plugin is
  the alternative for Claude Code.
- OpenCode facts verified on 1.18.35 and the `dev` snapshot
  (`docs/research/opencode-v2-integration.md`): the plugin hook object blocks
  by throwing; a `permissions` list in an agent file is ignored (the agent
  stays allow-all), so agents use the `permission` map; a Claude-style
  `tools: Read, Grep` makes a 1.x config invalid (2.x reads it); `skills`, `instructions`
  (frontmatter included), `commands/` and `command/` are all read. No `skills`
  or `instructions` entry is installed: the symlinks already work, and the
  plugin injects the posture each turn.
- OpenCode context: both hosts ask for the system context on every model
  request, so the plugin builds it once and reuses it until `.git/HEAD`, its
  reflog or `.git/index` change (stats, no spawn). A 10-turn scripted drive of
  the hook in this repo: 5,022 bytes a turn either way; a rebuild each turn
  cost 153 ms in all (13 ms a turn, a first turn of 34 ms), the cached plugin
  13 ms in all (the first turn only). The full text stays on every turn rather
  than a short reminder after turn 1: the repeated prefix is byte-identical so
  providers cache it, and a changed prefix would bust that cache for a saving
  of roughly 1,250 tokens (an estimate, the bytes divided by 4, not a
  tokenizer count). Not measured: provider cache hits in a live session
  (no model calls were made).
- OpenCode usage: on 1.x a plugin's `event` hook sees `cost` and `tokens`
  (input, output, reasoning, cache read/write) with `agent`, `modelID` and
  `providerID` on each `message.updated` assistant message; on 2.x
  `ctx.event.subscribe` yields `session.step.ended` and `session.usage.updated`
  with `cost` and `tokens`, and agent and model come from the `context` hook.
  The plugin records it into the same ledger
  (`skills/usage-it/scripts/opencode.mjs`), tokens only, one row per session
  with reasoning folded into `out`: on 1.x from the `event` hook, on 2.x from
  `ctx.event.subscribe`, with agent and model from the `context` hook. Limits:
  1.x marks a subagent by `parentID` on `session.created`, 2.x has no parent
  signal so every run is kind `session`; totals live in plugin memory, so a
  restart mid-session restarts that run. Event shapes are from the research
  note, run against fixtures, not a live session. On Claude Code the `Stop` and
  `SubagentStop` hooks already keep
  a per-run usage ledger from the transcripts (`skills/usage-it`, tokens only,
  no dollar estimate since prices change); it is not tied to a work item or step,
  but a step's usage can be read by time window (`usage.mjs --from/--to`).
- Org-specific material (Jira, `.compliance-rules/`) is configuration, not
  code: the repo works with neither.

## 9. Authoring rules

- Skill anatomy (addyosmani, trimmed): When to use / not use, Process, Red
  flags, Verification. Common-rationalizations table only for discipline
  skills that get skipped under pressure (tdd, audit).
- SKILL.md target 100 lines; detail in sibling files one level deep. Shared
  conventions live in one skill (`do-it/STATE.md`, `do-it/LANES.md`) and
  others link to them with `../do-it/...`.
- Descriptions: user-invoked get one human line; model-invoked get "what it
  does" + "Use when ..." with concrete triggers. Never summarize the process
  in the description.
- Routing evals in CI: each positive prompt ranks its skill first; fail on
  description pairs that are too similar (addyosmani tier 2).
- No em-dashes; the area's CONTEXT.md vocabulary; no AI attribution in anything that
  ships.

## 10. Decisions

1. **Build step name:** `build-it`.
2. **Commits:** none until ship; ship commits only on the user's "do it"
   (ADR-0002).
3. **Hooks:** standards and compliance hooks on by default (ADR-0004).
   OpenCode has no subagent hook; its plugin injects into every turn (the
   internal voice rules are not injected there; see Terse internal voice).
4. **Tracker:** a configurable seam, local by default, GitHub and Jira by
   config; user defaults with per-project overrides (ADR-0003).

## 11. Exploring existing and new projects

- **Scout before sizing.** `do-it` reads the code the request points at
  (`do-it/SCOUT.md`): new vs existing (mapped or unmapped), what already
  exists, reach, risk, overlapping work items. Never asks; names what it
  found in the lane line.
- **New projects** plan with `scope-it/GREENFIELD.md`: purpose, stack (via
  `look-it-up`), shape, quality bar, ADRs for foundation choices, and a walking
  skeleton phase that blocks the rest.
- **Exploration skills**, routed from `do-it` when the request is to
  understand rather than change (`do-it/EXPLORE.md`):
  - `map-it`: facts only, `docs/reference/` or chat (replaces `doc-it` phase
    1 and `zoom-out`); `/map-it <area>` also writes the area's `CONTEXT.md`
    (all but Terms) and its map row, and every run reports map drift.
  - `sweep-it`: pre-existing problems, ranked, concrete cases, files what the
    user picks (replaces `doc-it` phase 2 and the old `audit-it repo` mode;
    adds ponytail-audit's lenses).
  - `deepen-it`: upstream mattpocock `improve-codebase-architecture`, plus a
    hand-off to `do-it` or `log-it`.
  - `look-it-up`: mattpocock `research`, unchanged.
- **Project docs resolve per repo.** Context map (`CONTEXT-MAP.md`), context
  (`CONTEXT.md`), changelog, ADR and reference directories are detected or
  configured once (`resolveDocs` in the shared config) and injected into every
  session; skills keep naming the defaults.
- **One context per area, listed in a root map.** Every step reads the map,
  then the area's `CONTEXT.md` (identity, terms, relationships, key files,
  design notes). name-it writes Terms, map-it the rest; files and map rows
  are created lazily, never by a read-only step. GLOSSARY files are read
  only as a fallback (ADR 0005). The session code map leads with the map's
  tables, so a monorepo shows its areas first.

# Lanes over a fixed six-step chain

The Doc Cycle in rshingleton/skills ran issue, plan, implement, audit, verify and commit for every change, so a one-line fix paid for a plan directory, a grill and an audit report. do-it sizes each piece of work into a lane (XS, S, M, L) and runs only the steps that lane needs, with `/do-it` as the single entry. Each step stays callable on its own. The cost is a sizing judgement on every request; the rule "when unsure, pick the larger lane" and a list of risk areas that force at least S keep that judgement on the safe side.

---
status: accepted
---

# No commits until ship

Builds leave every change uncommitted in the working tree, and `ship-it` commits only when the user says so in that run. The owner reviews changes by hand, and per-phase commits broke that workflow; this reverses the commit-per-phase design (rshingleton/skills ADR-0011).

Amended in part by ADR [0008](0008-opt-in-run-commits.md): a `--complete` run may commit verified phases when the user asked for it with the flag. Outside a run this decision holds unchanged.

## Consequences

- Phase progress and audit results cannot be tied to commits. The state block records them, and `audit.fingerprint` (a hash of the diff since `base_ref` plus untracked files, excluding the planning directory) tells `ship-it` whether code moved after the audit.
- Parallel phases still need commits to merge. They run on scratch branches in separate worktrees and land on the user's branch with `git merge --squash` followed by `git reset`, so the user's history never sees them. Parallel mode only starts from a tree with no uncommitted code; once a phase is built in place, the rest follow in place.
- Untracked files do not appear in `git diff`; audit and ship list them explicitly.

---
status: accepted
---

# One tracker seam, layered dotenv config

Every tracker operation (create, get, comment, start, close, publish) goes through the `track-it` skill, backed by local files by default and by GitHub (`gh`) or Jira (REST v2) when configured. Configuration is dotenv files layered user, project, project-local, then environment, so a team commits its tracker choice and each developer keeps tokens out of the repo.

## Considered options

- **Port the Jira connector bridge.** It worked by echoing `CONNECTOR: ...` lines from bash for the agent to translate, and carried Jira-only assumptions into every skill. Replaced by a zero-dependency Node CLI with one adapter per tracker. When a Jira or GitHub MCP tool is present, the agent uses it for the same operation instead of the CLI.
- **YAML or JSON config.** Dotenv was chosen because the same file works as an environment file, needs no parser dependency, and matches the existing `JIRA_*` variable names.
- **Jira REST v3 (ADF bodies).** v2 with wiki markup works on Data Center and Cloud alike, which a v3-only client would not.

---
status: accepted
---

# Standards and compliance hooks on by default

do-it ships hooks for Claude Code (SessionStart, SubagentStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse) and an equivalent OpenCode plugin, enabled by default and disabled with `DO_IT_HOOKS=off`. Rules are split by who can decide them: anything a regex decides (secrets, env files, `.compliance-rules/checks.json`) is enforced by hooks on every edit and every `git commit`; judgement rules in `.compliance-rules/*.md` are checked by `prove-it`. HIGH findings block the edit; MEDIUM and LOW are reported back to the agent. Hooks fail open on crashes so a bug in a hook never blocks work, and a `do-it: allow` marker on a line covers false positives. prove-it's guardrail candidates feed new `checks.json` rules, so judgement findings that keep recurring become mechanical ones.

status: accepted

# Context files and a context map, not GLOSSARY files

mattpocock/skills renamed its domain-doc convention from `CONTEXT.md` /
`CONTEXT-MAP.md` to `GLOSSARY.md` / `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` (upstream d80fa0f) and
recorded no reason. do-it keeps the CONTEXT names: an area's file holds more
than terms (identity, relationships, key files, design notes), so "glossary"
undersells it, and the repos do-it works in (amp) already use a root
`CONTEXT-MAP.md` with one `CONTEXT.md` per area. Following upstream would
have meant renaming those files and losing the richer shape; GLOSSARY files
are still read as a last fallback so mattpocock-style repos keep working.

## Execution notes

- The resolver keeps `DO_IT_GLOSSARY` as an alias of `DO_IT_CONTEXT`, so
  existing configs keep working.
- A dry run of map-it against amp found area files with headings outside
  the five-section shape ("Domain Concepts", "Status"). Such sections are
  kept as written, and one that defines domain words counts as Terms.
- The plan's phase 1 text said the map appears "when a second area gets a
  context", which contradicted the decision that the first area below the
  root creates it; the audit caught it and the decision won.
- Open notes from the audit: a prose-only `## Relationships` heading shows

  step; ship-it's DOCS.md can still create a context file for new terms; the
  manifest list lives in both `hooks/lib/codemap.mjs` and CONTEXT-FORMAT.md;
  the code map comment and a test fixture use amp as the example; indented
  headings and escaped pipes are not handled in the over-budget path.

# Repo config files are untrusted for commands and endpoints

A repo's `.do-it/config.env` and `.do-it/local.env` are written by whoever controls the repo, and the hooks are on by default (ADR 0004). So two keys from those files apply only after the user has trusted their exact values: `DO_IT_LINT_CMD`, which the hooks run in a shell after every edit, and `JIRA_BASE_URL`, which receives the user's Jira token. `tracker.mjs trust` records a hash of the values (not the path) in the user's config directory; a changed value needs trusting again, and every clone or worktree with the same values shares one trust. Until then the user, environment or default value applies and the session notice names the ignored keys. Other keys stay as ADR 0003 describes them.

## Considered options

- **Trust the repo path.** An allowlist of repo roots is simpler, but a pulled commit could change the command with no review, and each worktree would need its own entry.
- **Never read these keys from repo files.** Safest, but it breaks the documented team setup, where one committed file carries the tracker URL and lint command for everyone.
- **Leave it.** Opening an agent in a cloned repo would then run that repo's chosen command, and send the user's token to its chosen host, with no prompt.

## Consequences

- Each developer runs `tracker.mjs trust` once per repo, and again whenever a teammate changes either value; setup-it offers it.
- `DO_IT_HOOKS=off` from a repo file is still honoured: turning checks off is a team choice, not code execution.

## Execution notes

- The same work closed the commit-scan bypasses from the 2026-10-19 sweep.
  The scan reads the commit's words with a small shell lexer (quotes,
  `$(...)`, heredocs, `$'...'`, redirects, `cd`/`pushd` before the commit),
  and whenever it cannot resolve the command for sure (unexpanded `$`, `~`
  or backticks in `-C` or a path, a failed git listing, paths matching
  nothing) it scans every tracked change from the repo root. Errors
  over-scan, never under-scan; the cost is an occasional block caused by an
  unrelated tracked file.
- Commits the hook does not recognise at all (after a newline, in a chain,
  behind `env` or `VAR=x`) and a relative `cd` after one that does not
  persist are open as T65; a redirect before the paths is T66.
- Audit Should items left as they are: the lexer could move to its own
  module with direct tests; `invalid()` in `checks.mjs` has three return
  states; `loadConfig` exposes trust internals (`config.trust`, unmasked
  values) to callers; a failed root listing is a silent allow (fail open);
  one trust hash covers both keys, so changing either needs a new trust.

---
status: accepted
---

# One intake skill, two stores

Work was entered through `log-it` (issues) or `todo-it` (one-line to-dos), and
the user had to decide which before typing. `log-it` is now the only skill:
it sorts each item into an issue or a to-do from the text, defaults to a
to-do when unclear, and also lists, reviews, closes and promotes both.
`todo-it` is removed.

The stores stay separate. Issues have status, acceptance criteria, a log and
possibly a GitHub or Jira ref; to-dos are lines that vanish when closed. One
backlog file would break remote trackers, lose per-issue status and bodies,
and make every add edit the same file. A wrong call is cheap to undo:
promoting a to-do to an issue files it properly, and an unclear item landing
as a to-do costs a line, where a wrong issue costs a remote ticket.

`track-it` stays a separate seam: it is called by the build flow to fetch and
close issues by ref, which is not intake. The combined list reads local
issues through `tracker.mjs list`; GitHub and Jira issues are not listed.

## Execution notes

- `list --status` takes open, closed or all; `in-progress` counts as open.
  A local `close` deletes the issue file, so `closed` only matches old files.
  Files in the issues directory with no title are skipped.
- Routing eval after the merge: 95.5% (threshold 90%). `log-it` now ranks
  first for 8 of 10 positives, and its longer description pulls one
  `name-it` prompt toward it; watch this when either description changes.
- Remote (GitHub, Jira) issues are not in the combined list; `list` says so.

# Opt-in run commits

ADR [0002](0002-no-commits-until-ship.md) keeps every build uncommitted until `ship-it` commits on the user's word, because the owner reviews changes by hand. A complete run (`/do-it --complete`) chains many slices with no user turn between them, so one end-of-run diff cannot be reviewed or reverted by phase. A run that was started with `--complete` and a commit mode may therefore commit each verified phase, and each lane S slice, on the current branch when it is unprotected, else on `do-it/<roadmap-slug>`. The flag is the user's explicit ask; without it ADR 0002 holds unchanged. Each commit follows a passing `verify-phase`, stages by path after a boundary check, and is tagged `do-it/<id>/phase-N` for rollback. Nothing is pushed, amended or forced, and a run never opens a PR. Committing per edit, auto-pushing and staging everything were rejected: they flood history, publish unreviewed work and sweep in stray files.

## What it reverses and keeps

- Reversed, only inside a `--complete` run that names a commit mode: a verified phase or slice may be committed before `ship-it`. The run flag overrides `DO_IT_COMMIT=never` for that run.
- Kept: no commit without that flag, no push, amend, force or PR, parallel scratch branches and squash merges, and `ship-it` as the only step that commits outside a run.

## Consequences

- Phase progress can now be tied to commits in a run; the state block and fingerprint still record the verified baseline, and `fingerprint` and `review-diff` must stay correct across commits after `base_ref` (proved in phase 1 of complete-run-lane).
- The commit guard and the `<id>: ` message rule apply to run commits unchanged.
- Rollback is a local tag and a reset the digest names; the user still decides when to push.

## Execution notes

Built as complete-run-lane; the audit passed on round 4. Non-blocking findings, all filed in `docs/TODO.md` (T135 to T153):

- Run commits stage whatever `--paths` names; a directory path can sweep in other slices' edits. The commit gate checks that `verify-phase` passed, not that code is unchanged since. A retried phase commit throws on the existing tag after the commit lands, and the branch switch and record writes precede `git commit`.
- Lane M in `slice` commit mode commits its code once after its last phase verifies, then the closing docs (run-lane-hardening R4). The final review's `<base>...HEAD` is empty with `--commit none`.
- Caps: the audit-round cap stops a slice whose fifth round passed, and `run next` ignores `max_slices`.
- Fixed in the build: the closing-docs commit (`run commit --docs`, lane M and S), assumption merging (`run add-assumptions`), digest assumption keys (`<id>#<n>`), rejection after close (`run reject-assumption`), and the recorded run `base`.

# The usage ledger records tokens, never cost

`usage-it` and the OpenCode usage path write one ledger row per run with input, output and cache token counts, and no price. A report that wants a cost applies a price table when it reads the rows. Prices change, differ by plan and by model, and are easy to get wrong, so a stored cost would go stale in every old row while the token counts stay true. Storing cost beside tokens and recording cost alone were both rejected: the first freezes a guess into the data, the second loses the figure that can be re-priced.

## Consequences

- The digest and the `usage-it` report state counted tokens and never an estimate of money or time saved.
- Changing a price needs no migration; a new table re-prices every row.
- A cost field in a row is a defect, not a feature to fill in.

# A slice shipped with its Verify unmet does not block its dependents

A roadmap slice can ship with its Verify clause not met: the product defect it exposed is filed as an issue, and the slice is marked `shipped <date> <id>, Verify unmet: <clause>`. `work.mjs roadmap` counts such a slice as done, so a slice that depends on it is ready, and the unmet clause is listed beside that dependent. Holding every dependent until the clause is met was rejected: one filed defect would stall the whole run, and the defect has an issue that owns it. Hiding the unmet clause was rejected too: a reader must see what was not proven.

## Consequences

- Done means shipped or dropped; one predicate serves `next`, `blocked` and `blocking`.
- The unmet clause appears in the `roadmap` output next to each dependent and in the closing message, so the gap is visible at the point it matters.
- A dependent that truly cannot work without the unmet clause says so in its own Blocked-by, as a decision.

What this code does: skills (Markdown instructions), hooks and Node scripts
that run a size-scaled issue, plan, build, audit, ship flow in Claude Code and
OpenCode. The hooks run on every agent tool call; the scripts keep work-item
state in uncommitted plan files and talk to local, GitHub or Jira trackers.
Load assumed: one developer per machine, hooks on every tool call, several
sessions or worktrees on one repo at once, and repos that may be cloned from
someone else.

Read: hooks/, .opencode/plugins/, scripts/, skills/*/scripts/, tests/, all
28 SKILL.md files and their sibling docs, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/adr/.
Not read in full: jira.mjs request paths beyond what tests touch, codemap.mjs
past the first 60 lines, scripts/lib/routing.mjs.

guard-it scan over the whole history clean (11 built-in rules; no

## Findings

### Must

1. **A cloned repo's committed config can run commands and redirect Jira tokens** (`skills/track-it/scripts/config.mjs:70-110`, `hooks/lib/guard.mjs:45-52`, `skills/track-it/scripts/adapters/jira.mjs:28-40`)
   - **What this is:** `.do-it/config.env` in the repo is read after the user's own config and can set any key.
   - **Problem:** It can set `DO_IT_LINT_CMD`, which the hooks run with `shell: true` after the agent's first edit, and `JIRA_BASE_URL`, which receives the user's `JIRA_API_TOKEN` in the `Authorization` header. Only secret-looking keys warn. Validated: confirmed; ADR 0003 and 0004 do not cover untrusted repos.
   - **Fix:** Ignore command and endpoint keys (`DO_IT_LINT_CMD`, `JIRA_BASE_URL`, any future URL or command key) from project scope unless the user config trusts that repo root.
   - **If we skip it:** Opening an agent in an untrusted clone with hooks on (the default) is code execution and credential theft.

2. **A malformed `checks.json` blocks every edit in OpenCode and silently disables all checks in Claude Code** (`hooks/lib/checks.mjs:72,79,91,100`, `.opencode/plugins/do-it.mjs:28-57`)
   - **What this is:** `loadChecks` trusts each rule's shape; the OpenCode plugin has no try/catch and signals a block by throwing.
   - **Problem:** A rule with `"files": ".ts"` throws `rule.files.some is not a function`. Reproduced: Claude hook exits 0 ("failed open"), OpenCode `tool.execute.before` rejects, so the write is blocked. In Claude Code the same throw also drops session context and every built-in secret rule with only a stderr line.
   - **Fix:** Validate rule shape in `loadChecks` (drop non-objects, coerce `files` to an array, ignore bad severities with a warning); wrap each OpenCode hook body so an unexpected error allows.
   - **If we skip it:** One typo in a team's rules file stops all OpenCode edits, against the "hooks fail open" rule in AGENTS.md.

3. **The commit scan misses pathspec commits and `-a` before the first commit** (`hooks/lib/guard.mjs:65-100`)
   - **What this is:** Before `git commit`, the hook scans the staged diff (or `git diff HEAD` with `-a`).
   - **Problem:** `git commit -m x a.js` commits the unstaged working-tree `a.js`, but only `--cached` is scanned. With no commits, `git diff HEAD` exits 128, the error becomes `''`, and the commit is allowed. Validated: confirmed in a temp repo.
   - **Fix:** With pathspecs or `-i`/`-o`, diff those paths in the working tree; with no HEAD, diff against the empty tree (`EMPTY_TREE` in `changeset.mjs`).
   - **If we skip it:** Secrets written by a Bash command reach a commit unscanned.

### Should

4. **The local tracker will rewrite any `.md` file and drops list fields** (`skills/track-it/scripts/refs.mjs:15`, `skills/track-it/scripts/adapters/local.mjs:25-43`)
   - **What this is:** Any ref ending in `.md` is a local issue; `readIssue` keeps only flat `key: value` lines and `writeIssue` writes back only those.
   - **Problem:** `tracker.mjs comment docs/planning/x/README.md` (or `start` on an issue with a `labels:` list) silently drops the nested `phases:`/`audit:` block or the list. Plans are uncommitted (ADR 0002), so git has no copy.
   - **Fix:** Refuse refs outside `DO_IT_ISSUES_DIR`; refuse to write when the frontmatter had lines the parser skipped.
   - **If we skip it:** A wrong ref destroys a plan's progress record with no recovery.

5. **Plan and issue writes are not atomic, and `verify-phase` writes back a stale copy** (`skills/do-it/scripts/state.mjs:435`, `adapters/local.mjs:43`, `skills/do-it/scripts/work.mjs:224-241`)
   - **What this is:** Files are written in place with `writeFileSync`; `verify-phase` loads the item, runs the checks (minutes), then writes.
   - **Problem:** A kill or full disk mid-write leaves an empty plan; any `event` or `set` from another session during the checks is overwritten.
   - **Fix:** Write to a temp file and rename; re-read the item after the command, before the transition.
   - **If we skip it:** Lost progress in exactly the multi-session setup build-it's parallel mode creates.

6. **GitHub Enterprise URLs lose their host, so writes go to github.com** (`skills/track-it/scripts/refs.mjs:8-9`, `adapters/github.mjs:11,23`)
   - **What this is:** An issue URL is reduced to `owner/repo` and passed as `gh -R owner/repo`.
   - **Problem:** `https://ghe.corp/o/r/issues/5` acts on `github.com/o/r#5` when the user is logged in there; the comment on line 7 says GHE is supported.
   - **Fix:** Keep the host and pass `-R host/owner/repo`.

7. **Parallel implementers record phases without the verification gate** (`skills/build-it/PARALLEL.md:58`, `skills/do-it/STATE.md:24,34`, `work.mjs:95-104,224-241`)
   - **What this is:** build-it's serial path uses `verify-phase`, which runs the checks and records only on exit 0; PARALLEL.md tells implementers to call `event phase-done <n> "<commands>"`, which records a self-declared pass.
   - **Problem:** The gate exists for the one mode most likely to skip checks. The rule also lives in work.mjs, though state.mjs says all transition rules live in `transition()`.
   - **Fix:** Point PARALLEL.md at `verify-phase`; make `phase-done` reachable only from it.

8. **DESIGN.md describes the per-phase-commit model that ADR 0002 reversed** (`docs/DESIGN.md:16-26,64,80-83,95,207-208,226-235`)

# Caveman terse contracts: token baseline

Measures whether the voice block and report contracts (work item
`apply-caveman-terse-contracts-to-internal-agent-communicatio`) save tokens.
Single workload, one run per side, so the numbers catch a regression or a
large win, not a small one.

## Workload

Three read-only agents started from the main session, briefs verbatim. The
lane-S dry run in the plan is dropped: it writes files and is hard to repeat.

| Agent | Brief |
|-------|-------|
| `it-scout` | Where does the hook decide which subagent types skip the coding posture, and what does each branch inject? Give paths and line numbers. Under 150 words. |
| `it-reviewer` | Review commit 7ae5158 (git show 7ae5158) against its own message: does the change do what the message says? One finding per line. Under 200 words. |
| `it-skeptic` | Claim: in hooks/claude.mjs, read-only subagent types never receive any voice or style rules from the hook. Try to prove it false. Under 150 words. |

Repeat on the same commit's tree (checkout `7ae5158` content for the review
brief; the briefs name it). Each brief starts with a marker word
(`BASELINE-...`; use `AFTER-...` the second time) so the transcripts can be
found with `grep -l`.

## Method

`usage-snapshot` (below) sums the `usage` fields of a subagent transcript
under `~/.claude/projects/<repo>/<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, once per
distinct API message. Columns: input, cache write, cache read, output.
Cost-relevant: output and cache write; cache read is cheap and grows with
turns.

## Before

Date 2026-10-21, repo at `7ae5158` plus the uncommitted plan files; no
agent, hook or skill change yet.

| Agent | Turns | Input | Cache write | Cache read | Output |
|-------|-------|-------|-------------|------------|--------|
| it-scout | 4 | 8 | 12569 | 28382 | 65 |
| it-reviewer | 4 | 8 | 17728 | 39002 | 69 |

Date 2026-10-21, same briefs with `AFTER-` markers, after phases 1 to 3

| Total | Turns | Cache write | Cache read | Output |
|-------|-------|-------------|------------|--------|

## Verdict

Not proven (still the verdict; see the follow-up at the end of this section). The totals moved the right way, but one run per side cannot
separate the change from variance: the biggest movers (cache read, 37% down
for scout, 51% down for skeptic, 37% up for reviewer) track how many turns
each agent happened to take, not the text. Cache write, the cost of the
injected context, is flat to slightly down: the voice block (about 200
tokens) did not show up as a cost, because it went into the agent file in
place of the reviewer's own two rules and the hook skips `it-*`. Outputs
were already about 70 tokens, so the shape and caps had little to trim on

Kept: the contracts and caps cost nothing measurable and guard against the

To settle it, repeat on a workload with longer reports, several runs per

```js
// usage: node usage-snapshot.mjs <session.jsonl> ; sums usage per main transcript and each sibling subagents/agent-*.jsonl
import fs from 'node:fs'; import path from 'node:path';
const main = process.argv[2];
function sum(file) {
  const t = { turns: 0, input: 0, cache_write: 0, cache_read: 0, output: 0 };
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const line of fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n')) {
    if (!line.trim()) continue;
    let j; try { j = JSON.parse(line); } catch { continue; }
    const u = j.message?.usage; if (!u) continue;
    const id = j.message.id ?? j.uuid; if (seen.has(id)) continue; seen.add(id); // one API message can span lines
    t.turns++; t.input += u.input_tokens ?? 0; t.cache_write += u.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0;
    t.cache_read += u.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0; t.output += u.output_tokens ?? 0;
  }
  return t;
}
const rows = [['main', sum(main)]];
const dir = path.join(path.dirname(main), path.basename(main, '.jsonl'), 'subagents');
if (fs.existsSync(dir)) for (const f of fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.jsonl'))) {
  let type = f; try { type = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, f.replace('.jsonl', '.meta.json')), 'utf8')).agentType ?? f; } catch {}
  rows.push([type, sum(path.join(dir, f))]);
}
console.log('who\tturns\tinput\tcache_write\tcache_read\toutput');
for (const [w, t] of rows) console.log([w, t.turns, t.input, t.cache_write, t.cache_read, t.output].join('\t'));
```

# Caveman: source and flow

Answer: Caveman 4.x ships its voice as three self-contained skills (caveman, ultracave, megacave), tracks the mode per session in small files written by Node hooks, and re-injects the full skill at SessionStart, on mode switch, to subagents, and as a short reminder every prompt. ### 2. Flow: activation, state, hooks, intensity, off

- Intensity levels no longer exist as levels. The six levels (lite, full, ultra, wenyan variants) were replaced in 3.1.0 by three skills that map 1:1 to stored modes: `caveman`, `ultracave`, `megacave`, plus one-shots `commit`, `review`, `compress`, and `off`. Legacy values map forward on every read (`lite`/`full` to caveman, `ultra` to ultracave, `wenyan*` to megacave); writes never emit them. ([src/hooks/caveman-config.js](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/src/hooks/caveman-config.js), lines 39-66; [docs/technical/three-skills-refactor.md](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/docs/technical/three-skills-refactor.md), Goal and Mode model)
- The difference between levels is the entire skill file that gets injected. SessionStart reads `skills/<mode>/SKILL.md`, strips frontmatter, and emits the whole body under the banner `CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — mode: <mode>`, then the line `Switch: /caveman, /ultracave, /megacave. Off: "stop caveman" or "normal mode".` ([src/hooks/caveman-activate.js](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js), `buildRuleset`; [src/hooks/caveman-config.js](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/src/hooks/caveman-config.js), `loadRuleset` line 811, `rulesetBanner`)
- Skill lookup order: `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, then `../../skills/<id>/`, then `../skills/<id>/`. With no skill file found it falls back to a hard-coded ruleset of the nine rule headlines. ([src/hooks/caveman-config.js](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/src/hooks/caveman-config.js), `skillPathCandidates`, `fallbackRuleset` line 840)
- Hooks registered by the plugin: SessionStart, SubagentStart (`--subagent`), UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd (stats `--record`). All run `node` scripts and exit 0 if node is missing. ([.claude-plugin/plugin.json](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/.claude-plugin/plugin.json), `hooks`)
- Default mode resolution order: env `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE`, then repo-local `.caveman/config.json` or `.caveman.json` (walked up from cwd, first file that names a `defaultMode`), then user config (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/caveman/config.json`, `~/.config/caveman/config.json`, `%APPDATA%` on Windows), then `caveman`. `manual` is a startup policy (sessions start off, explicit `/caveman` activates); `off` suppresses automatic and bare-command activation. ([src/hooks/caveman-config.js](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/src/hooks/caveman-config.js), header comment and `getDefaultMode` line 174; [skills/caveman-help/SKILL.md](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/skills/caveman-help/SKILL.md), "Configure Default Mode")
- Headless `claude -p` and Agent SDK sessions (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` starting `sdk-`) start under `manual` unless `CAVEMAN_DEFAULT_MODE` is set. ([src/hooks/caveman-activate.js](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/blob/bad48a0e1df55e05e3f52249afa35ecc1909ee76/src/hooks/caveman-activate.js), `startMode`)
- Mode state is per session: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-sessions/<session_id>.mode` (plus `.prev` for one-shot restore), keyed by the `session_id` in the hook payload. `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.caveman-active` remains as a last-write-wins mirror that never holds the literal `off` (deactivation deletes it). Session ids are whitelisted before use in a path. ## Swept roadmap, every decision in a legal state

Fixture: a one-slice-blocked roadmap (`R1` blocked by `D1`, `R2` free) with
`D1` under Open decisions, swept as `weak-but-explicit` the way
[SWEEP.md](../../skills/roadmap-it/SWEEP.md) §2 says: the default recorded as an
assumption in the run record (`run add-assumptions walk sweep`), nothing else.

- `work.mjs run next` offers `R2` and never `R1`; after `R2` ships it has
  nothing left to offer for `R1` either.
- `work.mjs roadmap` still reports `R1` `blocked`, "waiting on D1", and
  `finished: false`.

So a decision the sweep has settled is still an open one to the roadmap. The
run ends with `R1` neither shipped nor parked, and `run next` does not list it
under `parked` or `waiting`, so the closing message has nothing to say about
it. The live run hit the same thing: R12, R16 and R22 were held back by D3, D2
and D1 until the three were moved to Decisions so far by hand.

A `ready` decision is legal (dated line, removed from Open decisions). A
`weak-but-explicit` one has no such step in SWEEP.md, which is silent about
Open decisions for it, so it is not legal as written. An `ask-when-reached` one stays in
Open decisions by design, but the slice it blocks is left unparked and
unreported, which is the same gap.

and shipped through `work.mjs` (the scope-it

Defects the walk found:

Our five agents can be generated as `.opencode/agents/it-*.md` with `mode: subagent`, a `permissions` list instead of `tools`, and no pinned model. Newly found gaps: v2 does not read `CLAUDE.md`, does not read `.claude/agents`, a custom subagent does not inherit parent permissions, subagent depth defaults to 1, and per-step cost and tokens exist in the server API (not in a documented plugin hook). # What is current in OpenCode v2 for plugins, skills, commands, agents, config and rules, and which farmage/opencode-skills examples should do-it adopt?

Answer: OpenCode v2 loads plugins from a `plugins` array (or `.opencode/plugins/`) and expects a `Plugin.define({id, setup})` default export; it ignores the v1 `server()`/hook-object shape, so T9 needs a second export, not a config edit. v2 reads `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, uses `commands/` (plural, `command/` still found), and agents carry `model` plus `permissions` (no `tools`). Of farmage, only the dev-link idea and validation targets are worth adopting; its install copies and its plugin-cache doc are not. Confidence: medium (hook payloads read from source types, blocking semantics and the v2 `context` system shape not verified by running).

Versions: OpenCode stable release feed shows v1.19.3 (2026-10-16) as latest on anomalyco/opencode; v2 tags exist (v2.1.2) and v2 docs list `ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:2.0.0`. v1 object exports need 1.18.29 or later. farmage/opencode-skills at main.  Checked: 2026-10-21.

Config key is `plugins` (array of package names, local paths, or `{package, options}` objects) in `opencode.json(c)`; relative paths resolve from the config file; arrays from all config files are layered lowest to highest precedence. `.ts`/`.js` files and package directories directly in `.opencode/plugins/` or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` are auto-discovered; a root `plugins/` is not. Entries prefixed `-` disable an id or wildcard. https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/plugins/ (Loading).
- Plugin loading, v1. Key is singular `"plugin"`; dirs `.opencode/plugins/` and `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ (Config key, Plugin directories).
- v2 export shape. `export default Plugin.define({ id, setup(ctx) })` from `@opencode/plugin`; `setup` may return cleanup; options in `ctx.options`; Effect variant uses `effect()`. For dual support, default-export one object that spreads `Plugin.define({...})` and also carries a v1 `server()` function. V2 reads `id` and `setup()` and ignores `server()`; v1 hooks are not translated. https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/ (Plugin definition, Differences from V1). Also packages/plugin/src/README.md at https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/README.md (raw via gh api contents).
- v2 hook registration is per domain: `ctx.<domain>.hook(name, cb, {providerID?})`, returning a registration with `dispose()`. Plugins run in order. https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/ (Hook registration).
- v2 hooks that map to ours:
  - `ctx.session.hook("context", ...)`: runs each agent-loop model call incl. tool continuations; edits `system`, `messages`, `tools`, `options`; reads `agent`, `model`, `sessionID`. Replaces v1 `experimental.chat.system.transform`. Source types: `SessionContext` has `system: Array<SystemPart>` (not a string array), https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugin/src/promise/session.ts.

Event payloads may carry usage but the event type list is not given in v2 docs. https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/ (Tokens, usage, and cost). v1 docs also list no usage data; v1 `message.updated` event exists (https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ Events) but its payload fields were not shown.

Inference (mine, not stated by sources):

- T9: do-it's `.opencode/plugins/do-it.mjs` exports only `DoItPlugin` returning v1 hooks. Under v2 it would either be skipped or fail the `Plugin.define` check. Fix is a default export that spreads a `Plugin.define({id: "do-it", setup})` object and keeps `server`. `setup` would register `ctx.session.hook("context")` (push our text onto `system`, mind it is `SystemPart[]`), `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")` (throw to block, assumed from v1; semantics unverified), and `execute.after` (append to `result`, shape of `Tool.Result` not read). `decide()` stays shared. The header comment's `{"plugins": [dir]}` for v2 is consistent with the docs, but a dir under `.opencode/plugins/` is auto-discovered, so install-hooks could skip the config edit for project installs.
- Auto-discovery risk: v2 loads direct `.js` files in `.opencode/plugins/`; our `.opencode/plugins/` ships `do-it.mjs` in the repo, so opening do-it itself in v2 may load it without any config. Check that it fails open.
- Usage issue (docs/issues/per-step-usage-record-on-do-it-work-items.md): no documented v2 plugin hook exposes per-step token usage. Realistic options: document the gap for OpenCode, or read usage through `ctx.event.subscribe` or the client API after confirming payload fields in source. Do not promise parity yet.
- No subagent hook in either version: our "subagents share the system hook" note stays true, and in v2 the `agent` field on `context` could let the plugin skip injection for the main agent only if needed.
- Install gaps: `scripts/install.sh` writes commands to `.../opencode/command/` (singular) and links `.opencode/command` generated files. v2 prefers `commands/`; singular still works, so no break, but a v2-first install should target `commands/` and gen-opencode could emit it (v1 reads `command/`, so keep both or detect). Our commands emit `$ARGUMENTS` and a `description` only, which is valid in v2.
- Skills: our `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` links are both read by v2 and v1 (v2 docs list both); linking to both risks duplicate IDs for the same skill, worth a test on a real v2 install. Our skill `name` fields equal directory names, so path-derived IDs match.
- Agents: `agents/` files are Claude-format (`tools`, model tiers) and install only to `~/.claude/agents`. OpenCode v2 would need `permissions` frontmatter and `provider/model` ids, so reusing them is not free; leave as a gap.

- Adopt: `dev-link`/`dev-unlink` pattern with `.bak` backup, as `scripts/install.sh --dev` or a npm script. Our install already symlinks, so the new part is only the `.bak` restore; low value, optional. Ties to the install gap.
- Adopt: a `check` target that also validates skill frontmatter and docs sync. We already have `npm run check`; no gain.
- Adopt idea: `instructions` array plus `skills` array in opencode.json as the v2-native way to point at repo rules and the skills dir without symlinks. Ties to T9: the installer's opencode.json merge could add `skills: [<clone>/skills]` instead of linking into `~/.agents/skills`. Needs a v1 check (v1 `skills` key not verified).
- Adopt idea: skill permission rules and `disable-model-invocation` for typed skills, since v2 honours it. Ties to our typed vs automatic skills; verify our frontmatter already sets it.
- Do not adopt: `install.sh` copy approach (stale copies, uninstall leaves commands), the plugin-cache symlink doc (wrong host layout), MODELAGENTS.md text (copied superpowers material, conflicts with our it-core posture and the repo rule not to copy other repos' text), AGENTS.md skill limits (their 1024-char and 80-100 line figures differ from our SKILL-MECHANICS budget).

## v2 plugin types (2026-10-21)

The npm `dev` plugin package has no `session` or `tool` hooks, but
`@opencode-ai/plugin@beta` (0.0.0-beta-19271) and `@next` do (the `dist/promise`
files). Read from those types, and the plugin is written to them:

- `Context` has `location.directory`, `session`, `tool`, `permission`, `event`.
  There is no `ctx.directory`; the plugin now uses `ctx.location.directory`.
- `session.hook("context")` event: `{sessionID, agent, model, system:
  SystemPart[], messages, tools, generation, providerOptions}`. `SystemPart` is
  `{type: "text", text, cache?, metadata?}`.
- `tool.hook("execute.before")` event: `{tool, sessionID, agent, messageID, id,
  input}` with `tool` and `input` mutable.
- `tool.hook("execute.after")` event: the same fields plus `status:
  "completed"` with `result`, or `status: "error"` with `error`.
- `Tool.Result` is `{output?, content?, metadata?}`; `content` is a string or
  a list of `{type: "text", text}` or file parts. It is not a string
  `output`, so the plugin appends its note to `content` (string: appended,
  list: a text part pushed, absent: set).
- `permission.hook("evaluate")` event: `{sessionID, agent?, action, resources,
  effect, message?}`.

The `opencode-ai@beta` npm binary (0.0.0-beta-202608110357) is the v1 CLI and
does not host these hooks; OpenCode 2.1.2 (brew) does, see the next section.

# Terse voice: paired headless A/B

Third attempt at the question in [caveman-baseline.md](caveman-baseline.md) and
[terse-voice-ledger.md](terse-voice-ledger.md): did the voice block and report
contracts (`35df34e`) lower what `it-*` subagents cost? This one runs the same
five briefs on both trees, five times each, in isolated headless sessions on
the logged-in account, and scores whether findings survive. Run 2026-10-27.

## Verdict

**No evidence of a saving on these cases, and no dropped finding detected.** The voice change did not make runs cheaper here; whether it makes them costlier is not resolved.

- Total input per run is flat: -10% to +7% across the four `it-*` cases, and
  +2% on the control. The `after` tree adds about 700 to 860 input tokens to
  every run, the control (a general agent the voice hook skips) included, so
  that overhead is not the voice block's alone.
- Output tokens were higher in the `after` arm in three of four cases (prove
  +13%, scope +31%, sweep +27%) and lower in review (-6%); report words moved
  -17%, +20%, +6%, +5%. Every range overlaps its pair, and the control's
  spread is about 6%, so the direction is suggestive (not lower) but not
  resolved. Sweep cost is +16% (median 0.114 vs 0.098 USD).
- Keyword recall of eight planted defects (four of them negation findings),
  scored on review, prove and sweep, was 8 of 8 in every run of both arms
  except one `before` sweep run that missed one (7 of 8). Scoring matched a
  file name plus a keyword and was not read one by one, and the raw reports
  were not kept, so this shows no dropped finding was detected, not that every
  finding was described correctly. Scope and the control are not scored.

Kept, as decided before: the voice block and contracts guard against long
reports. This run does not show them saving tokens on reports that were
already short (a 300-word cap, about 250 words returned). The earlier "not
proven" verdicts are replaced by this one.

## Method

- Arms: `before` is a git worktree at `35df34e^` (`7ae5158`: the `it-*` agent
  files without a voice block, the old hook); `after` is a worktree at
  `9a28943`, the tree at the time of the run. The `it-*` agent files differ
  between the arms only by the voice change, but the hooks and the rest of the
  tree differ by 60-odd later commits, so the A/B measures the tree, not the
  voice block alone; the control (a general agent the voice hook skips) shows
  how much of a difference comes from outside it. Each run started in its own
  worktree.
- Isolation that keeps the login: `claude -p --setting-sources project
  --output-format json --model sonnet` from the worktree, with no `--bare`
  (that skips OAuth). Each worktree held a `.claude/settings.json` whose hooks
  were the checkout's own `hooks/hooks.json` with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`
  replaced by the worktree path, and `.claude/agents` linked to its `agents/`.
  `--setting-sources project` drops `~/.claude/settings.json` and so the
  global hooks, and the user-level agents did not load. Checked on a pilot per
  arm from the transcripts: the voice marker was absent from `before` and
  present in `after`, and neither transcript named `~/.local/share/do-it`.
- Permissions: `--allowedTools` for `Agent`, `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` and a few
  read-only `Bash(git -C *)`, `ls`, `cat`, `wc`, `cd` patterns, plus
  `--add-dir` for the fixture. No bypass mode.
- Driver: the main session was told to start the named agent
  (`it-reviewer`, or `general-purpose` for the control) with the brief
  verbatim and return its report verbatim. The briefs mirror the spawn
  paragraphs and report shapes of `review-it`, `prove-it`, `scope-it`
  (builder check) and `sweep-it`; the skills themselves were not loaded, so
  both arms share skill text by construction. `look-it-up` starts a general
  agent that the voice hook does not touch, so the fifth case is a control
  (a general agent summarising the fixture) and doubles as the noise
  estimate.
- Fixture: a 30-file repo (`main`, then a `feature` commit, 557 diff lines)
  with eight planted defects: unvalidated input (negation), off-by-one paging,
  swallowed write error, un-awaited charge (negation), missing ownership check
  (negation), unbounded retry (negation), ISO strings compared as text, SQL by
  concatenation. The commit message claims the validation, the ownership check
  and the retry limit, so those findings depend on a negation. Recall counted
  a defect when the report named its file and one of its keywords; a hit was
  not read for correctness one by one.
- Runs: 5 per case per arm, 50 in all, ten at a time (five cases, two arms)
  per round. Metrics per run: the sum of subagent `usage` over distinct API
  messages in its transcript (turns, input, cache write, cache read, output),
  the words in the returned report, and `total_cost_usd`.
- A first full pass was discarded: in some `review` runs the subagent's `Bash`
  was denied and it reported that it could not read the diff. The briefs were
  changed to read the diff and commit message from files and all 50 runs were
  repeated. No run in the reported set failed or was dropped.

## Results

Medians, range in brackets. `Total in` is input plus cache write plus cache
read.

| Case | Arm | Turns | Total in | Out | Words | Cost USD (median, range) |
|------|-----|-------|----------|-----|-------|----------|
| review | before | 2 (2-2) | 24,992 (24,992-24,992) | 918 (896-949) | 282 (265-299) | 0.053 (0.052-0.115) |
| review | after | 2 (2-2) | 25,718 (25,718-25,718) | 864 (781-1,013) | 235 (225-315) | 0.052 (0.042-0.115) |
| prove | before | 2 (2-2) | 24,679 (24,679-24,679) | 662 (608-739) | 216 (203-259) | 0.054 (0.048-0.108) |
| prove | after | 2 (2-2) | 25,405 (25,405-25,405) | 748 (565-863) | 260 (183-293) | 0.053 (0.026-0.112) |
| scope | before | 4 (3-5) | 46,203 (33,161-60,973) | 1,388 (1,249-2,142) | 346 (328-403) | 0.067 (0.042-0.078) |
| scope | after | 4 (3-4) | 49,639 (34,319-53,323) | 1,823 (1,263-2,101) | 368 (325-404) | 0.056 (0.043-0.076) |
| sweep | before | 10 (5-10) | 147,375 (60,239-167,673) | 2,706 (1,694-4,548) | 291 (222-337) | 0.098 (0.083-0.131) |

| control | before | 2 (2-2) | 50,128 (50,127-50,439) | 426 (367-451) | 129 (107-149) | 0.043 (0.023-0.062) |

After vs before, medians: total in +3%, +3%, +7%, -10% (review, prove, scope,
sweep); output -6%, +13%, +31%, +27%; words -17%, +20%, +6%, +5%. The control
moves -6% on words and 0% on output with no voice involved, so the noise is
about that size.

Keyword recall of the eight planted defects (review, prove, sweep, five runs each):
`before` 8, 8, 8, 8, 8 / 8, 8, 8, 8, 8 / 8, 8, 7, 8, 8; `after` 8 in all 15.

## Limits

- Cache write is not comparable per run: runs in the same round share an
  identical prefix, so the first run of an arm pays the write and the others
  read it (median 0 on most cases). Cost has the same problem, which is why the
  verdict rests on total input, output and words.
- Reports were already short: the caps (300 to 500 words) bind, and the agents
  returned 200 to 350 words. A workload whose reports overrun the caps could
  still show a saving; this one cannot.
- The noise line is read off one control (about 6% on words, 0% on output),
  which does not bound the 27% and 31% output moves in sweep and scope; those
  are called unresolved, not noise.
- One fixture, one main-session model (Sonnet), five runs a side, so a
  difference near 10% is not resolved. The scope and sweep ranges are wide.
- Main-session input growth after a report lands was not measured
  separately; the `total_cost_usd` and the returned-report word counts stand
  in for it.

The harness (driver, fixture generator, analysis scripts) was throwaway and is
not kept; the method above is enough to rebuild it.

# Terse voice: before and after in the usage ledger

Second attempt at the question in
[caveman-baseline.md](caveman-baseline.md): did the terse voice block and
report contracts (`35df34e`) lower what `it-*` subagents cost? The headless
A/B in `docs/issues/prove-or-refute-token-savings-of-the-terse-voice-change-with.md`
could not run: a headless `claude -p` in an isolated config dir is not logged
in and no API key was set, and the real config dir would load the global
`~/.claude` agents into both arms. This note uses real runs from the usage
ledger instead.

## Method

- Source: `~/.claude/do-it/usage/*.jsonl` (`skills/usage-it`), snapshot taken
  2026-10-26. One row per agent run: turns, output (`out`), cache write
  (`cc`), cache read (`cr`).
- Rows: every `it-*` agent run, 418 in all.
- Cut: the commit time of `35df34e`, 2026-10-21 10:59:24Z. Before: 25 runs.
  After: 393 runs. A control keeps only after-side runs from 2026-10-21, so
  the same day's work shows apart from later work.
- Per agent and side: n, median and range. A difference under about 10% is
  noise, the bar the A/B issue set.
- The script was throwaway and is not kept; the numbers recompute from the
  ledger with the filter above.

## Results

Medians, range in brackets.

| Agent | Side | n | Turns | Out | Cache write | Cache read |

| it-reviewer | after, same day | 59 | 4 (2-16) | 61 (19-2,008) | 19,929 (8,512-65,466) | 43,556 (6,622-747,343) |
| it-reviewer | after, all | 320 | 4 (2-18) | 2,188 (19-14,708) | 24,673 (8,512-91,631) | 58,025 (6,622-971,951) |
| it-scout | before | 3 | 3 (1-4) | 65 (3-377) | 12,569 (7,211-12,638) | 17,883 (0-28,382) |
| it-scout | after, all | 5 | 12 (6-18) | 9,222 (6,090-10,272) | 36,521 (28,079-64,215) | 272,694 (99,796-580,673) |
| it-skeptic | before | 2 | 5 (4-6) | 137 (52-222) | 13,433 (11,213-15,653) | 41,744 (27,399-56,089) |
| it-skeptic | after, all | 0 | - | - | - | - |
| it-planner | before | 1 | 3 | 2,687 | 18,764 | 25,732 |
| it-planner | after, same day | 2 | 12.5 (5-20) | 3,319 (37-6,601) | 37,192 (24,712-49,671) | 371,663 (70,054-673,272) |
| it-planner | after, all | 5 | 12 (5-20) | 6,601 (37-14,146) | 49,671 (24,712-68,789) | 307,530 (70,054-673,272) |
| it-builder | after, all | 63 | 20 (7-77) | 21,017 (5,202-63,119) | 95,636 (36,026-657,402) | 1,669,274 (321,677-13,418,267) |

`it-builder` has no before side: the `it-*` agents were created the same
morning as the voice change. The same-day control has runs only for
`it-reviewer` and `it-planner`; `it-scout`, `it-builder` and `it-skeptic` have
none that day.

## Verdict

Not proven, and the ledger cannot prove it. Not refuted either.

- The one comparison with real counts is `it-reviewer` on the same day: turns
  4 vs 4, output 60 vs 61, cache write 22.7k vs 19.9k (12% lower, n 19 vs 59),
  cache read 47.5k vs 43.6k (8% lower). Output and turns are flat; cache write is
  just outside the 10% noise line and cache read inside it. That agrees with
  [caveman-baseline.md](caveman-baseline.md): the reports were already short,
  so the voice block has little to trim, and it does not show up as a cost.
- Every other row is confounded. The after side is dominated by later work
  (full audits, builds) whose reports are far longer than the before runs:
  the `it-reviewer` median output moves from 60 to 2,188 across the same
  agent, which the voice change does not explain; the work mix is the likely cause,
  not checked. `it-scout`, `it-skeptic` and `it-planner` have 0 to 5 runs a side.
- The before side is 25 runs from one morning, and it likely includes the
  baseline runs made with the change in the working tree before it was
  committed, so the cut may leak in both directions.

Kept, as before: the voice block and contracts add no measurable cost and
guard against long reports. A real answer needs paired runs of the same work
on both trees.

Superseded 2026-10-27: [terse-voice-ab.md](terse-voice-ab.md) ran those paired
runs and replaces this verdict: no evidence of a saving, no
dropped finding detected.

# Backlog hardening

## Destination
The open bugs and debt found in the 2026-10-19 repo audit, the open issues
and the 2026-10-25 handoff review are cleared in an order that protects users
first, and OpenCode token work is measured before it is optimised. This
repo's hooks, tracker, flow state and checks do what the docs say.

- G1: No secret reaches a commit or a patch unscanned by the hooks, and the hooks still fail open and finish inside their timeout.
- G2: No tracker operation destroys or misroutes an issue or a plan.
- G3: The flow's state and hand-offs behave as documented: a fix round records its verification, retro-it can reach the audit's guardrail candidates, and a closing line names a step the user can run.
- G4: `npm test` and `npm run check` enforce what AGENTS.md and the skills claim, and do not depend on the developer's environment.
- G5: Each rule and each parser lives in one place, and the docs describe the model that ships.
- G6: OpenCode pays for session context once and can record usage, with token claims measured before anything is optimised.
- G7: A finding the flow surfaces (an audit's Should and Nice, a product defect a verify slice exposes) is offered to `log-it` at ship, not lost when the plan is deleted, and a slice whose verify clause is unmet says so.
- G8: An open roadmap decision is asked and settled before the slices it blocks are stranded, never silently skipped by `next` or `/do-it`.
- G9: The in-hunk dev-null twin of R2 is closed, so a unified hunk cannot steer a scoped rule either.

## Milestones

Slices share files (`hooks/lib/guard.mjs`, `scripts/check.mjs`, `skills/ship-it/`),
and concurrent uncommitted work items invalidate each other's audit (T49), so
build one slice at a time, in id order within a milestone.
